result.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response when sync mode is active (`const response = await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...); return response;`), but the caller then does `const token = res?.data;` — a fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and `googleCredentials.access_token`/`expiry_date` are set to undefined and persisted via prisma.credential.update, silently destroying the credential. Verifiable mechanism directly from the diff.

judged_text: Google Calendar sync-mode refresh reads .data off a raw fetch Response, making token undefined and persisting undefined access_token/expiry_date, silently destroying credentials; also missing response.ok check on sync endpoint response

adjudication.rationale: In GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` can return a raw `fetch` Response when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` (see `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`). Immediately after, the code does `const token = res?.data;` and reads `token.access_token` / `token.expiry_date` (see `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`), but a fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token` will be undefined and this will throw or break token refresh. Additionally, the sync-path fetch has no `response.ok`/status handling in `refreshOAuthTokens`, so non-2xx responses aren’t detected before use. (Separately, Google Calendar now stores the return value of `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`—a Zod safeParse result—into `credential.key`, which is also incorrect.)
